lyrics: Sun beats down on    a twisted spine.
Ninety-nine years, doin'    devil's time.
Hand full of cotton,    soul full of stones.
Sweat and the sorrow deep in my bones.
This muddy water, it's the
only home I've known.
Parchman Farm is a shadow long.
Singin' to the rhythm of    what's gone wrong.
Boss man's ledger, a list of sins.
Every day you lose, every day he wins.
The dice are loaded 'fore    the game
even begins.    Yeah,
I'm Delta born and Delta bred.
Got the Mississippi River runnin' through my head.
This ain't just the blues, it's the truth being said.
In the bottom of a bottle and    a piece of stolen
bread.
Friday night, the old juke joint shakes.
Healin' up the pieces of    what the week
takes.
A beat-up guitar and    a gut-bucket groan.
Tellin' everybody they ain't    sufferin' alone.
Plantin' a seed in this hard,
bitter stone.
Hear the whistle blowin' on the northbound
train.
A whisper of Chicago in    the drivin'
rain.
Some say it's freedom, some say it's just a trade.
For a different kind of trouble and a different kind of blade.
But it's a dream you can hold when the other ones
fade.         Yeah,
I'm Delta born and Delta bred.
Got the Mississippi River runnin' through my head.
This ain't just the blues, it's the truth being said.
In the bottom of a bottle and    a piece of
stolen bread.
Yeah, this muddy water...
It's the only home
I know...
But that whistle's callin'...
And           a man's just got to
go...
... A man's just
got to go.
